paragraphs.title: Opening the Psalm and Asking God to Listen

easy.explanation: The psalm is identified as a psalm of David.
easy.q: To whom is the psalm attributed?

answers: Listen to his words and prayer
easy.explanation: He asks the LORD to give ear to his words and hearken to his cry.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do?

easy.explanation: He says, “unto thee will I pray,” addressing the LORD.
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist say he will pray?

answers: Only the words of his enemies
medium.explanation: The verses mention his words, meditation, voice, and cry.
medium.q: What does the psalmist ask God to hear?

medium.explanation: In this context, meditation refers to the psalmist’s thoughts and inward reflections.
medium.q: What does “meditation” mean in “consider my meditation”?

answers: He is speaking only to a human ruler
He recognizes the LORD as his ruler and God
He wants to turn away from God
medium.explanation: These titles show the psalmist’s personal devotion and submission to God.
medium.q: What is emphasized by calling the LORD “my King, and my God”?

answers: They emphasize his request for careful attention
They command his enemies to be silent
challenge.explanation: Both expressions intensify the request that God listen attentively.
challenge.q: How do “Give ear” and “Hearken” relate to the psalmist’s request?

answers: The psalmist describes only outward actions
He approaches God with words, thoughts, and urgent pleas
He does not want to speak to God
challenge.explanation: The prayer includes spoken words, inward thoughts, and a desperate cry.
challenge.q: What does the sequence of words, meditation, and cry suggest?

answers: Prayer is part of the psalmist’s regular beginning of the day
He is speaking only about the weather
challenge.explanation: The repetition presents morning prayer as a deliberate and regular practice.
challenge.q: What does the repeated reference to the morning in verse 3 suggest?

short_answers.question: What does the psalmist ask God to consider?
short_answers.explanation: He asks God to consider his inward thoughts and reflections.

short_answers.question: What titles does the psalmist use for God in verse 2?
short_answers.explanation: These titles express loyalty and personal faith.

short_answers.question: When will the LORD hear the psalmist’s voice?
short_answers.explanation: The psalmist says that God will hear his voice in the morning.

paragraphs.title: Morning Prayer and Choosing the Good Path

answers: At the end of the year
easy.explanation: Verse 3 twice refers to the morning, when he directs his prayer to God.
easy.q: When does the psalmist direct his prayer to the LORD?

answers: He directs his prayer to God and looks up
easy.explanation: He says, “in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist do in the morning?

answers: A God who delights in wickedness
easy.explanation: Verse 4 says that God does not take pleasure in wickedness.
easy.q: What kind of God is the LORD described as not being?

answers: Prayer places the psalmist before God and directs him toward what is right
The two ideas have no connection
medium.explanation: His morning prayer expresses dependence on God and a desire to follow His will.
medium.q: How are morning prayer and choosing the good path connected?

medium.explanation: Looking up conveys expectation, hope, and attention toward God.
medium.q: What does “look up” suggest in this context?

answers: To seek God’s guidance and approval
medium.explanation: The prayer shows his desire to begin the day under God’s direction.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist begin the day by directing his prayer to God?

answers: Prayer is a consistent part of the psalmist’s routine
The psalm is mainly about weather
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes regular, intentional prayer at the start of the day.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the repeated mention of the morning?

answers: God does not delight in wickedness, and evil cannot dwell with Him
The verse makes no distinction between good and evil
challenge.explanation: The verse presents God’s character as completely opposed to wickedness.
challenge.q: How does verse 4 contrast God with wickedness?

answers: The psalmist carefully presents and arranges his prayer before God
challenge.explanation: To direct the prayer suggests presenting it deliberately before the LORD.
challenge.q: What does the verb “direct” communicate about the prayer?

short_answers.question: What does God not take pleasure in?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 4 says that God has no pleasure in wickedness.

short_answers.question: What does the psalmist direct to God in the morning?
short_answers.explanation: He directs his prayer to the LORD and looks up.

short_answers.question: What cannot dwell with God?
short_answers.explanation: The verse states that evil shall not dwell with God.

easy.explanation: The verse says that God has no pleasure in wickedness.
easy.q: What does God not delight in?

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “The foolish shall not stand in thy sight.”
easy.q: Who shall not stand in God’s sight?

easy.explanation: Verse 6 refers to the bloody and deceitful man.

answers: Foolish people, workers of iniquity, liars, and violent or deceitful people
Only those who pray in the morning
medium.explanation: The passage names the foolish, workers of iniquity, liars, and bloody and deceitful people.
medium.q: What kinds of people are rejected in this passage?

medium.explanation: The expression means to live or remain in God’s presence.
medium.q: What does “dwell with thee” mean in this context?

answers: Because they practice wickedness, falsehood, violence, and deceit
medium.explanation: Their sinful actions and dishonest speech separate them from God’s favor.
medium.q: Why does God reject the people described in these verses?

answers: Both show that evil is incompatible with God’s presence
Both describe the joy of the wicked
Both teach that God approves of iniquity
challenge.explanation: God rejects wickedness and therefore does not permit the wicked to stand before Him.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between “thou hast no pleasure in wickedness” and “the foolish shall not stand in thy sight”?

answers: His speech is dangerous and destructive
challenge.explanation: The image portrays the destructive and deadly effect of his words.
challenge.q: What does the image of an open sepulchre suggest about the wicked person’s throat?

answers: Their tongues flatter, but their inward part is wicked
They do not speak at all
challenge.explanation: Their smooth speech hides inward wickedness and deceit.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the enemies’ tongues and their inward character?

short_answers.question: Who shall not stand in God’s sight?
short_answers.explanation: The verse says that the foolish shall not stand in God’s sight.

short_answers.question: What does God hate according to verse 5?
short_answers.explanation: The verse directly states that God hates all workers of iniquity.

short_answers.question: What is described as an open sepulchre?
short_answers.explanation: The enemies’ throat is compared to an open grave because of the danger of their speech.

paragraphs.title: Entering God’s House and Seeking Guidance Against Enemies

answers: By the multitude of God’s mercy
By the strength of his enemies
easy.explanation: He says he will come into God’s house through the multitude of God’s mercy.
easy.q: By what does the psalmist come into God’s house?

easy.explanation: He says, “in thy fear will I worship toward thy holy temple.”
easy.q: How does the psalmist worship in God’s holy temple?

easy.explanation: He asks the LORD to lead him in righteousness and make His way straight.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do?

answers: Because he wants to leave God’s house
Because he wants to praise falsehood
medium.explanation: He asks to be led in righteousness because of his enemies.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask for guidance?

medium.explanation: The temple is presented as the holy place toward which he worships.

answers: They speak falsely, plot evil, and flatter
medium.explanation: Their mouths lack faithfulness, their inward parts are wicked, and they flatter with their tongues.
medium.q: What qualities are attributed to the enemies in this passage?

answers: Mercy grants him access, while reverence expresses his respect for God
Mercy causes him to despise God
challenge.explanation: He enters because of God’s mercy but worships in fear and reverence.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between God’s mercy and the reverence shown by the psalmist?

answers: Guide him along a clear and upright path
Make the path full of deceit
challenge.explanation: The request is for clear direction and a righteous way before him.
challenge.q: What does “make thy way straight before my face” mean?

answers: Their falsehood, plotting, and flattery are part of their wrongdoing
challenge.explanation: The psalmist describes their corrupt speech and rebellion before asking God to judge them.
challenge.q: Why is the request for judgment connected with the enemies’ speech?

short_answers.question: By what does the psalmist enter God’s house?
short_answers.answer: By the multitude of God’s mercy.
short_answers.explanation: He recognizes that access to God comes through divine mercy.

short_answers.question: What does the psalmist ask God to make straight?
short_answers.explanation: He asks God to make the divine way clear and straight before him.

short_answers.question: What is in the enemies’ mouths according to verse 9?
short_answers.explanation: Their speech is characterized by falsehood and untrustworthiness.

paragraphs.title: The Joy of Those Who Trust and God’s Protection of the Righteous

answers: All those who put their trust in God
easy.explanation: The verse says that those who trust in God will rejoice and shout for joy.
easy.q: Who will rejoice and shout for joy?

easy.explanation: God defends those who put their trust in Him.
Verse 12 says, “thou, LORD, wilt bless the righteous.”

answers: Because they turn away from Him
medium.explanation: Their joy is grounded in God’s protection and defense.
medium.q: Why do those who trust in God rejoice?

medium.explanation: The image describes God surrounding the righteous with protection and favor.
medium.q: What does “compass him as with a shield” mean?

answers: As surrounding them with favor like a shield
medium.explanation: God blesses the righteous and surrounds them with favor.
medium.q: How is God’s attitude toward the righteous described?

answers: Both describe people who are devoted to and dependent on God
challenge.explanation: The verse joins trust in God with love for His name as marks of faithful people.
challenge.q: What is the connection between those who love God’s name and those who trust in Him?

answers: God’s defense produces joy, and His favor rests upon the righteous
The righteous are punished for rejoicing
Those who trust in God turn away from Him
challenge.explanation: The passage links divine protection, joyful worship, and blessing.
challenge.q: What does the movement from rejoicing to blessing suggest?

challenge.explanation: The shield image presents God’s favor as a protective covering around the righteous.
challenge.q: What does the image of God surrounding the righteous like a shield communicate?

short_answers.question: Who will rejoice and shout for joy?
short_answers.answer: Those who put their trust in God.
short_answers.explanation: Their joy comes from God’s defense and protection.

short_answers.question: Whom will the LORD bless?
short_answers.explanation: The final verse directly promises blessing for the righteous.

short_answers.question: With what does God compass the righteous?
short_answers.answer: With favour as with a shield.
short_answers.explanation: God’s favor is pictured as a protective shield surrounding the righteous.
